evals.expected_output: Should ask clarifying questions about scope. Should NOT generate a full plan or start researching from a vague prompt.

assertions.text: Asks what specifically needs improvement or what area of the codebase to target
Does NOT write a plan file to thoughts/shared/plans/
Does NOT spawn codebase research agents before understanding the request

evals.prompt: /create-plan Fix the typo in CLAUDE.md line 15 where 'componets' should be 'components'
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this task is too small for a formal plan and suggest doing it directly instead of creating a multi-phase plan.

assertions.text: Recognizes the task is trivial and does not warrant a formal multi-phase plan
Suggests fixing the typo directly or with a simpler approach rather than creating a plan
Does NOT create a multi-phase implementation plan for a one-line fix

evals.prompt: /create-plan Add a caching layer to the user service so that repeated lookups by ID don't hit the database
evals.expected_output: Should research the fixture project, produce a plan with phases that are independently committable, with verifiable success criteria referencing real code.

assertions.text: Reads the actual user_service.py file before planning (not just assumes its contents)
Plan references actual function names, class names, or line numbers from the fixture project — not hallucinated ones
Each phase can be committed and tested independently — no phase depends on completing a later phase
Success criteria contain actual runnable commands (e.g., 'make test', 'pytest tests/') not vague descriptions like 'verify it works'
'What We're NOT Doing' section contains specific items relevant to the task (not generic boilerplate)
Plan saved to thoughts/shared/plans/ with YYYY-MM-DD naming

evals.prompt: /create-plan Add real-time WebSocket notifications to the REST API. The system must remain stateless with no server-side session storage, but WebSocket connections need to persist user state between messages.
evals.expected_output: Should identify the contradiction between stateless requirement and WebSocket state persistence, and ask for clarification before planning.

assertions.text: Identifies the tension or contradiction between 'stateless' and 'WebSocket state persistence'
Does NOT silently pick one interpretation and plan around it without flagging the conflict
Presents design options for resolving the conflict (e.g., external state store, token-based state, etc.)
Asks for user input on how to resolve the conflict BEFORE writing a full plan

evals.prompt: /create-plan Refactor the data_processor module to use the strategy pattern instead of the current if/elif chain
evals.expected_output: Should analyze the actual if/elif chain, identify all 5 branches, and propose incremental refactoring that maintains backward compatibility at each step.

assertions.text: Plan identifies all 5 format branches in the current if/elif chain (json, csv, key_value, xml_simple, fixed_width)
Each phase maintains backward compatibility — existing callers and tests work throughout the refactoring
First phase adds or verifies characterization tests before making structural changes
Does NOT propose replacing the entire if/elif chain in a single phase
Desired End State section describes what the code looks like after refactoring, not just 'it uses strategy pattern'

evals.expected_output: Should read the ticket file fully, research the codebase, discover the auth dependency, and produce a plan addressing all 4 acceptance criteria from the ticket.

assertions.text: Reads the ticket file completely (not partially) before starting research
Plan addresses all 4 acceptance criteria from the ticket (bulk_import method, summary return, update existing SKUs, error collection)
Discovers or mentions the auth module (auth.py) and considers whether bulk import needs permission checks
Presents plan structure or findings and asks for buy-in BEFORE writing the full detailed plan
Final plan has no open questions — all decisions are made (or flagged for user input before writing)
